item.title: Destiny brought Mauricio Pochettino to Man United - but one huge question remains
item.description: On Sunday evening, Mauricio Pochettino got the call he had been waiting for. He and long-time assistant Jesus Perez had frequently asked about Manchester United over the last decade. They would often contact friends in the game who were connected to Old Trafford , looking to find out what was happening, whether there could be an opening. Pochettino came very close to taking one of those openings on at least three occasions: 2018, 2021 and 2024. Now, elements might finally have aligned. It is a call that others at Old Trafford have long waited for, too. Back when they had a much publicised dinner in 2016, Sir Alex Ferguson essentially told Pochettino he should be the United manager. The Argentine was enthralled at that meeting by stories from one of the game’s great glory eras, and a sense of magic he had felt just standing in Old Trafford had been deepened. Pochettino had been especially taken by Ferguson’s account of rebuilding United from the 1980s, initially drawing comparisons with what he was doing at Tottenham Hotspur . Now, he’s set to take on that exact same job, if one that has become so much bigger than in 2016 . It is arguably even bigger than in 1986. Pochettino, however, is fired by the idea of being the man to finally fix United. It has become one of the great managerial quests. The United hierarchy have ultimately gone for him because of that personality, and his standing. They don’t want a coach who hasn’t worked at this level. They want someone ready. Both the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe can sense that, since the two sides of the United ownership have known Pochettino for years. If this is an appointment that always felt destined, though, that does raise one big question. Is this the right moment for it? Is it like Jose Mourinho , in that it came too late? Is it typical of modern United in that sense? Is it the same old “magical thinking” of hoping a famous name saves them, when the game has changed and the actual problems are now so structural? Mauricio Pochettino's Tottenham were one of the great Premier League teams (Getty) Pochettino probably should have gone to United in 2016 or 2018, when he was at a peak in terms of being one of the most exciting coaches in football. The club did consider a move in the summer of 2016, but sources say an exit clause was allowed to expire. How different things could have been. Old Trafford insiders are now talking about the value of “a name”, but the hierarchy did pass on Pochettino in 2024, when they initially considered sacking Erik ten Hag before ultimately decided to stick with the Dutchman. His interview wasn’t seen as convincing as that of Thomas Tuchel or Roberto De Zerbi. Those who know him also say he is closer to being “a manager” now, in terms of a wider outlook, rather than the on-the-grass coach that so drove Spurs. item.title: Is England v Croatia on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch Nations League clash
item.description: England resume their Nations League campaign needing just a point from their last two fixtures to qualify for the quarter-finals in March. Thomas Tuchel’s side take on Croatia at Wembley Stadium and will be full of confidence given they won the last meeting between the two teams 7-0 only last month. The Three Lions are three points behind leaders and World Cup winners Spain in group A3 and have the best goal difference in the group, having scored 14 and conceded three - all to Spain - in their fixtures in this campaign so far. They take on the world champions in their final fixture of this group stage, while Croatia will face the Czech Republic, with both games on Sunday. Here’s everything you need to know. When is England v Croatia? England take on Croatia at Wembley Stadium on Thursday 12 November, with kick-off at 7.45pm GMT. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch the match live on ITV1, with coverage from 7pm GMT. A live stream will be available via ITVX. Team news Newly crowned Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane is set to mark his return to England duty in style; he will break the record he shares with Peter Shilton for all-time international appearances if he wins his 126th cap this week. Marc Guehi withdrew from camp with injury and Ezri Konsa is sidelined for the Croatia game, although it is hoped he will be fit to feature against Spain. Dan Burn and uncapped Bournemouth defender James Hill have come into the side as replacements. Jobe Bellingham and Fulham’s Josh King have been handed their first England call-ups , but Myles Lewis-Skelly is banned after accumulating too many yellow cards. Croatia will be without Ivan Perisic - absent for the same offence - as well as the injured quintet of Josip Sutalo, Martin Pongracic, Andrej Kramaric, Franjo Ivanovic, and Kristijan Jakic. item.title: France’s Antoine Dupont gamble reveals the truth about clash with South Africa
item.description: It would, in a different scenario, be a page out of the Rassie Erasmus playbook. Moving a scrum half of otherworldly play-making gifts to fly half? One can just imagine the Springboks supremo, who has challenged plenty of rugby’s conventions, licking his lips at the prospect were South Africa to develop a talent of that type. Of course, for France, necessity has been the mother of this intriguing invention. Antoine Dupont will wear the No 10 shirt for his country for the first time in Paris on Friday night not due to any tactical ingenuity but to an ever-deepening injury issue for Fabien Galthie . Gone, first, were the silkily-skilled Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos; so, too, a dependable enough deputy in Antoine Hastoy. Still, at least they had the experienced hand of Romain Ntamack at the tiller – until he went off with his arm in a sling against Fiji. Antoine Dupont will make his first Test start at fly half (PA Wire) And so it is left to Dupont to learn on the job against the world champions. A relatively regular fly half for Toulouse, the 29-year-old nonetheless awaits a baptism of fire. He can, at least, count on the steady presence of Maxime Lucu alongside him – an unintended benefit of the injury-enforced switch is that it gets two of France’s best individuals on the park together. "We took a lot of pleasure in tackling this challenge of designing something which could bring us greater stability and balance in our playmaking," Galthie explained. ”These are two players with a lot of experience, they are two icons in France and in the world, who we wanted to align together to lead the team on Friday night." Into the unknown, then, France and South Africa step. In this age of hybridisation, the possibilities presented by the dual scrum half system could yet prove fascinating. There is grand tradition of interchangeability in the halves within French rugby, after all. Equally, it feels a little like the hosts are entering this battle of international heavyweights with one arm behind their back. The task would be tall enough against the reigning champions of the world with a traditional 10 in place. Their injury problems do not solely dwell at fly half, either – how Galthie might like the mass and minds of Emmanuel Meafou and Thibaud Flament on a night like this. Emmanuel Meafou is another key French absentee (Getty) There are just six survivors in the French 23 from the team that started this fixture last November. Perhaps this injury-hit France squad are paying for the arduous calendar with which they have to contend. With clubs in France wielding significant financial and cultural power, the Top 14 now extends to a nearly 10-month season. It is little wonder that there is a high attrition rate as a result. item.description: The Oklahoma City Thunder fell apart in crunch time in a 118-108 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers on Wednesday. item.title: Thunder’s Mark Daigneault sounds off on factor that led to second straight loss to Blazers
item.description: Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images Thunder’s Mark Daigneault sounds off on factor that led to second straight loss to Blazers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Oklahoma City Thunder have had to soldier on this season amid an injury avalanche has left them quite shorthanded. With Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, and Cason Wallace already on the mend, Ajay Mitchell had to miss their Wednesday night clash against the Portland Trail Blazers. And with that, the Thunder simply did not have enough firepower as they lost their second-consecutive game against the Blazers, 118-108. OKC was still in the game during crunch time, but in the end, head coach Mark Daigneault admitted that Portland simply outplayed them when it mattered the most. “We played really hard tonight. I thought we really competed. I thought our execution was pretty good… Credit Portland. They made more plays down the stretch,” Daigneault said after the game, per Nick Gallo of FanDuel Sports Network. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) With 3:07 remaining in the game, the Thunder were down by just three points, 103-100, after Shai Gilgeous-Alexander split a pair on the charity stripe. But the Blazers would lock in and score on seven consecutive possessions to keep OKC at bay. It is not too often that any team gets their way against the Thunder’s elite defense. But in a make-or-miss league, Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard got the job done for Portland to sweep the mini two-game set on a back-to-back against OKC. As for the Thunder, they most certainly need more help on offense. Gilgeous-Alexander is facing a crowd on every possession, especially with OKC starting Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara, two paint-bound bigs on offense, sharing the court to start the game. This has caused a drop in scoring efficiency for the reigning MVP. It did not help that Jared McCain shot just 3-of-14 from the field to finish with just 10 points on the night. This Thunder team will still win plenty of games thanks to Gilgeous-Alexander’s greatness and the team’s strong defensive floor. But for them to buy enough time for their core players to potentially return from injury, the Thunder will need to perform better on offense to keep in step with their opponents. item.title: Pat Cummins calls press conference to address Usman Khawaja sandpapergate revelations
item.description: Australia captain Pat Cummins has called a press conference to have his say on Usman Khawaja’s ball-tampering allegations that have reopened the 2018 sandpaper scandal . Cummins has been rested from the white-ball series against England which begins on Friday in Perth , but has publicly invited a media grilling in Sydney on Friday morning to respond to the accusations which have followed the publication of Khawaja’s new autobiography. Khawaja’s memoir Sabr has reopened old scars in Australian cricket, specifically with his claims that knowledge of the sandpaper plot was widespread within the team and coaching staff even though Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft alone were punished. In an interview with the Sydney Morning Herald he said blame was shared by “all of us”, said his calls for collective responsibility were shot down by specific un-named team-mates and suggested tampering had been going on prior to the Cape Town Test where Bancroft’s cheating was exposed. His revelations have invited renewed speculation over the role of the bowling group which benefitted from the ball manipulation – with Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon having previously distanced themselves from the episode. In 2021, the quartet issued a carefully worded statement responding to “rumour mongering and innuendo” in which they denied knowing that a foreign substance had been taken on to the field to alter the ball. That line may no longer hold water, given Khawaja’s suggestions that the matter was openly discussed and had taken place in the previous match. Now Cummins, who could find his position as captain of the national team called into question, is set to confront the issue head on. Cummins (right) is set to respond to accusations made by Khawaja (left) (Adam Davy/PA) “I’m training at Cricket Central (in Sydney) tomorrow morning before the Blues play in the Shield match,” he wrote on X. “Happy to speak with any and all media about the events of this week at 9.30 am. I’ve taken some time to try and better understand the long list and full extent of Uzzy’s allegations so I can respond properly. Afterwards please stay and support the Blues! I’ll ask CA (Cricket Australia) to send out details.” Starc appeared at a sponsor’s event earlier this week, offering a stiff response that reiterated his previous position. “As far as our statement said, we weren’t aware of things being taken on the field, that’s where I’ll leave it,” he said. “I’ll stick to what I said five years ago, what I said at the time, eight years ago. Clearly, there’s different versions from different people, and I’ll leave it where I left it back then.”

item.title: “Whit Got SMOKED”: Fans Think Dan Lanning Won the Verbal Battle After His Response to Kyle Whittingham’s “Outbid Everybody” Comment
item.description: Dan Lanning Oregon © Reuters Oregon head coach Dan Lanning is currently preparing for war on Saturday, and he may have just given his biggest preview of it from the podium. On “Inside Michigan Football” on Monday, Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham offered this somewhat backhanded praise for Lanning: “Outstanding football coach… Tireless recruiter. He really does a great job recruiting, and it doesn’t hurt that you have $50+ million at your disposal to, in essence, outbid everybody.” When Lanning was asked about these remarks the following day, he said: “They’re spending more of their money right now on their coaches that they’re letting go, so maybe it makes it hard to sign players. But I know they’ve signed a couple of guys that we weren’t able to compete with what they decided to do, and maybe a lot of that money is tied up for them in another player. I don’t know.” That response garnered much fan support: Dan Lanning gets candid on Dylan Raiola’s development as Oregon starter In the same press conference on Wednesday, Dan Lanning shared his thoughts about how far Dylan Raiola has progressed as a starting quarterback: “I think he’s been a really good preparer throughout the season. But I did feel like I saw a difference when we were watching one reel. … Every time that happened last week, Dylan immediately was calling out the coverage before the ball was even snapped, recognizing alignments. I think that’s really helped him.” He continued: “He’s had that same breath and mindset this week. But he also looks back at that game and says, ‘Okay, here’s a really big growth moment. Here’s where I can really get better.’ … So his preparation, I’ve really liked watching it and seeing how he does it. He’s really developing his process, and it’s growing.” Kickoff for the Oregon-Michigan game is at 3:30 p.m. ET/12:30 p.m. PT on FS1. “Doesn’t Hurt That You Have $50+ Million Dollars at Your Disposal”: Kyle Whittingham Takes A Jab At Dan Lanning Ahead Of Michigan Vs. item.title: Charles Barkley calls out ‘dumb’ players while explaining point guard’s importance
item.description: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Charles Barkley calls out ‘dumb’ players while explaining point guard’s importance appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . NBA legend Charles Barkley was one of the league’s most lethal weapons during his heyday. He was a two-way machine with his strength, athleticism, and toughness. Most importantly, Barkley understood the game well and the role every player has on the floor. After the game between the Golden State Warriors and the Houston Rockets on Wednesday, Barkley praised Fred VanVleet for steering the ship since his return from an ACL injury. Barkley underscored his point by explaining the importance of a point guard. “The point guard, even if you’re not the best player on the team, you’re the most important player on the team by who you give the ball to and who you don’t give the ball to,” said Barkley on “Inside the NBA.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Hall of Famer then proceeded to call out players who do not recognize the value of a floor general. “People don’t understand how important the point guard is,” added Barkley. “Because all players are kind of dumb. When I say that, every player thinks he’s a superstar. They’re like, ‘Just give it to me!’ I’m like, ‘No, you can’t dribble!’ I’m gonna give it to you to finish, and that is so important.” Charles Barkley: "The point guard even if you're not the best player on the team, you're the most important player on the team by who you give the ball to and who you don't give the ball to. (FVV) has the ball most of the time, and people don't understand how important the point… pic.twitter.com/e5GiPat4U0 — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) November 12, 2026 The former MVP benefited from playing with floor orchestrators, most notably Maurice Cheeks on the Philadelphia 76ers and Kevin Johnson on the Phoenix Suns. He also played with Magic Johnson, John Stockton, Penny Hardaway, and Gary Payton on Team USA. Barkley claimed that the Rockets lacked direction when VanVleet was out last season, as they merely dumped the ball to Kevin Durant and Alperen Sengun and let them operate. The Rockets beat the Warriors, 115-108 , to improve to 9-3. VanVleet had 18 points on 6-of-9 shooting, including 4-of-7 from long distance, six assists, three steals, and zero turnovers. item.description: Trying to feed a dribble hand-off to Jared McCain, Deni Avdjia bulldozed his way to a steal. The former NBA All-Star had a wide-open path to the other side as he threw down the vicious dunk. That capped off another frustrating clutch-time outing for OKC as it fell down by double-digit points with 36 seconds to go. The Oklahoma City Thunder were out-dueled in clutch time with a 116-106 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers . They leave their two-night stay at Moda Center humbled by what their ceiling is with this patched-together group. Hoping for a Portland split, the Thunder went all in with their starting lineup. No messing around by staggering Alex Caruso. He received the ultra-rare starting nod. They played with much better energy from the jump. Understanding how dire their health was, Isaiah Hartenstein stepped up as a primary scorer. He Eurostepped his way to a layup. The Thunder had a 32-28 lead after the first quarter. As soon as it looked like they had control of the game's flow, the Trail Blazers raced back. They had a 24-8 run in the second quarter. Mostly fueled by outside jumpers. Everybody in Portland had a turn to hit a momentum-shifting 3-pointer. Meanwhile, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander couldn't get to the rim. Instead, he settled for highly-contested jumpers. That completely torpedoed OKC's offense. They only had 18 points in the second frame. They entered halftime in a 56-50 deficit to the Trail Blazers. Quite the emotional gut-punch if you're the Thunder. You went all out with your available supporting cast and it simply isn't enough. Under normal circumstances, Gilgeous-Alexander can afford an off-half. But not under these. That gets put under the microscope. Coming out of the break, the Thunder rediscovered some of their scoring magic. Specifically, Gilgeous-Alexander returned to playing like a walking 30-point bucket. He nailed a couple of elbow jumpers. He also finally drove to the basket. What a surprise — he finally went to the free-throw line with that scoring style. item.title: ‘It’s painful’ – Luka Doncic shares firsthand injury update after Lakers win over Bucks
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Doncic’s hot start to the 2026-27 NBA season might have been sidetracked by an injury in a 123-112 win over the Milwaukee Bucks. Doncic had a weak game by his standards but still ended the night with 32 points, five rebounds and five assists with two steals. The Lakers’ offence cratering without him led to coach JJ Redick leaving Luka in a 20-point game with under five minutes to go, leading to an injury. While the Lakers did manage to be outscored by 15 points in the time without Doncic to end the game, many have been worried they lost their MVP-caliber star to a potential absence. Luka Doncic shares a mixed message on injury after Lakers win Despite leaving the game with an injury, Doncic was available to speak to media members after the game, sharing a direct injury update. “I’m good. Obviously, it’s painful a little bit, but I’ll be fine. We got 3-0 on the road trip, so that’s very good.” Admitting he’s in pain while also saying he’s good is a mixed message, although it’s just Doncic illustrating that the injury is minor enough for him to continue playing. Doncic is averaging 38.6 points, 7.6 assists and 7.5 rebounds this season, so the Lakers need him to be healthy to have any hope of maintaining the best record in the NBA (11-2). This has been an early-season trend with Doncic for years, where his style makes him pick up minor injuries over the first few months before he inevitably misses time periodically from December to February. The Lakers will hope to avoid that fate with Doncic this season and will presumably manage him carefully. Unfortunately, with Austin Reaves also getting hurt against the Bucks, coach Redick might not have the liberty to give both his star guards extended rest to heal up from minor injuries. item.title: Luka Doncic’s, Austin Reaves’ injury scares dose of scary deja vu for Lakers
item.description: We all still have PTSD from April 2. In what was supposed to be a measuring stick game against the Thunder, Luka Dončić suffered a strained hamstring that sidelined him the entire postseason and Austin Reaves sustained a strained oblique that kept him out the first four games of the playoffs. Just like that, the Lakers were wiped off the board. Their two leading scorers were taken out amid a 16-2 run. Their chances of winning a championship were gone. It was over for the purple and gold. So, when Dončić and Reaves both suffered injuries in a 123-112 win over the Bucks , it was hard not to wince. Not again. Not now. Luckily for the Lakers, this was not that . Dončić said “I’m good” following falling to the floor and clutching his right ankle after Kyle Kuzma closed out on him as he made a 23-foot jumper in the fourth quarter. As for Reaves? His status is more uncertain after he suffered a left heel injury in the third quarter , subbed himself out three minutes later and didn’t return. Lakers coach JJ Redick said his X-rays were negative and that he will get imaging on Thursday. He added that his Achilles’ tendon is not a concern. Austin Reaves, who exited with a left heel injury, drives on Jericho Sims during the Lakers’ win over the Bucks on Nov. 11, 2026, in Milwaukee. Getty Images Luckily, this doesn’t seem catastrophic for a Laker team that has the best record in the league at 11-2 and has won seven straight games. At least this time, both of their superstars weren’t wiped out in the same game. But it was scary. It was a dose of deja vu. It was a reminder of how fragile all of this is. The Lakers have been the greatest surprise of the league this season. No one thought they’d be championship contenders. Not after LeBron James left. Not after they acquired nine new players. Not after there were questions around Walker Kessler after he missed all but five games last season because of shoulder surgery. The assumptions were unanimous: The Lakers needed time to develop chemistry. And they were still a piece or two away from competing, given their thinness at backup center and the question marks around their perimeter defense. item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 31: Malo Gusto of Chelsea acknowledges the fans after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge on October 31, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Chris Lee - Chelsea FC/Chelsea FC via Getty Images) | Chelsea FC via Getty Images We’re slowly approaching the January transfer window, and given that it’s the international break, there’s plenty of space for a few rumors to make their way around the footballverse. Of particular interest to us may be the story that Malo Gusto is said to be “open” to leaving Chelsea and is now “assessing his options” with three and half years still to run on his current contract (2030 expiry). The BBC are among those who nibbled a bit at this little rumor-nugget, adding that while Chelsea’s stance at the moment is “unclear”, we were shopping the 23-year-old around this summer already, at a £75m asking price. That’s a rather optimistic valuation, especially now that Manchester City cannot just make up income numbers (or can they?). Enzo Maresca was always a big fan of Gusto, and a reunion was speculated about before the season, but unlike in the case of Enzo Fernández, did not come to fruition. It probably won’t help Gusto’s valuation that he’s finding himself less and less involved as the season’s come along. He’s not started a league match for two months, and I don’t imagine too many are questioning those decisions from Xabi Alonso, unlike some of his other choices of late. Gusto’s substitute appearance against Sunderland was his 100th Premier League appearance, and 144th overall for Chelsea. He’s among our longest-serving players these days despite his young age — a testament to the constant chopping and changing of the team. Only Reece James and Wesley Fofana have been part of the first-team squad for longer. But throughout those 3.5 years, Gusto has failed to convince consistently, despite his versatility and world class speed. He’s had moments of great impact and could at times even be practically unplayable for the opposition with his fluid movement and lack of a defined position. But those moments have been few and far between. His best season for us was, perhaps, his very first, when he often thrived in Mauricio Pochettino’s chaosball. Since Poch is about to take over at Manchester United, perhaps they will be interested in another Chelsea castoff? Malo Gusto is open to a move away in January. The former manager recorded an 84% leadership rate, finishing 80 of his 95 matchdays at the top between 2017 and 2020. Flick is setting new standards at Barcelona. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) In terms of absolute numbers, Flick already ranks fourth among Barcelona managers, with Pep Guardiola leading the historical ranking with 87 occasions at the summit, followed by Frank Rijkaard with 85 and Valverde with 80. Barcelona’s title-winning seasons explain Flick’s remarkable numbers Flick’s record has remained impressive across all three campaigns. During his first season, Barcelona led the standings on 31 of 38 matchdays, representing 82%. That figure dropped to 26 occasions in 2025/26, equivalent to 69%, but the team still secured another championship. His current campaign has been even more dominant, as Barcelona have occupied first place on 11 of the 12 matchdays, giving Flick a 92% leadership rate in 2026/27. Flick guaranteed another week at the top of La Liga Flick enjoys a view from the top of La Liga table. item.title: ‘Who’s teaching him?’- Robert Horry tears into Walker Kessler’s offensive game with brutal assessment
item.description: Photo by Ben Liebenberg/Getty Images Robert Horry has delivered a brutal assessment of Walker Kessler’s offensive game, questioning the Lakers centre’s lack of post moves despite his seven-foot frame. Kessler has become an important part of Los Angeles’ strong start to the season after joining from the Utah Jazz. Luka Doncic backed the move, with the Lakers viewing the centre as someone who could fit their long-term plans. However, Horry believes there is plenty of room for improvement in Kessler’s work around the basket, particularly when it comes to creating his own shots. Robert Horry questions Walker Kessler’s lack of post moves Speaking on his Big Shot Bob podcast, the former Lakers star did not hold back when discussing the 24-year-old’s offensive limitations. “You know what’s really scary about Walker Kessler? Hey, I know guys in elementary got better post moves than him. He got no post moves, man. I’m like, who is teaching this dude any post moves? You’re seven f****** feet tall. Get you a little jump hook, man. You don’t have to dunk everything.” Horry also questioned Kessler’s tendency to pass out of offensive rebounds rather than take the opportunity to score himself. “I don’t even think he wants to score ’cause I’ve seen him get offensive rebounds and kick that out instead of crunching that. I’m like, dude, you’re 7 ft tall. Get you a power dribble. Go up and dunk that too.” The criticism comes despite Kessler settling into a role that the Lakers specifically brought him in to fill. Kessler has helped deliver that, with the Lakers enjoying one of the best records in the NBA. His ability to play alongside Doncic and Austin Reaves has been an important part of their early-season success. Horry’s comments also overlook the way the modern NBA operates. Kessler is often expected to move the ball to better scorers rather than force attempts when Doncic or Reaves are available. With Kevon Looney struggling to provide a reliable alternative at centre, Kessler’s role remains particularly important. The Lakers will need him to maintain his defensive presence and continue fitting into their offence as they look to establish themselves as genuine Western Conference contenders. item.description: Liverpool v Chelsea - Carabao Cup Fourth Round - Getty Images Sport Manchester United and Manchester City are monitoring Chelsea defender Malo Gusto as the west London club place a £75 million price tag on the peripheral right-back. The 23-year-old Frenchman has fallen behind Josh Acheampong in the Stamford Bridge pecking order since head coach Xabi Alonso took charge. Rivals monitor sidelined French full-back According to talkSPORT , both north-west heavyweights are tracking Gusto closely after his first-team opportunities diminished under the Blues' new Spanish tactician. Despite club captain Reece James remaining sidelined through injury , the former Lyon defender has not started a Premier League fixture since September 12. Instead, academy graduate Acheampong has increasingly been favoured on the right side of the backline. Limited minutes spark departure speculation Signed from his boyhood French club Lyon for a fee of around £26m back in 2023, the attacking full-back had previously been a regular fixture in the capital, racking up 144 appearances and scoring three goals across all competitions. However, he has been named in the starting XI for just three of his seven top-flight outings during the current campaign. Aside from those sporadic league minutes, the defender started all three of his side's Carabao Cup ties before their fourth-round penalty shootout elimination against Liverpool. That reduced involvement has alerted domestic rivals, with City having already explored a potential move over the summer in hopes of sealing a reunion between the player and former Stamford Bridge boss Enzo Maresca. Financial verdict complicates Etihad pursuit Although the Etihad Stadium hierarchy remain keen admirers of his profile, the broadcaster notes that their ability to finance a £75m deal is complicated by ongoing off-field regulatory proceedings. Maresca's side are still awaiting the final outcome of their appeal after being found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules. An independent commission adjudged that the club had artificially inflated their revenue by £900m via 'sham' contracts over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. With a decisive sanctions hearing still pending and the result of their legal challenge yet to be confirmed, any pursuit of a big-money signing in the upcoming market is far from straightforward. Managerial transition clouds winter approach Meanwhile, United find themselves at a crossroads at Old Trafford after agreeing a deal in principle for United States boss Mauricio Pochettino to replace Michael Carrick . Given that impending dugout change and City's ongoing legal battle, it remains unclear whether either suitor will lodge an official approach when the January window opens. Nevertheless, Gusto's situation will be watched closely if he remains out of favour.

item.title: 'I'd tape it to my thumb': Ex-Australia star admits to using sandpaper after Usman Khawaja's revelations - WATCH
item.description: The Sandpapergate controversy has resurfaced in Australian cricket, eight years after the 2018 scandal. Following fresh revelations by former Australia batter Usman Khawaja in his memoir, 'Sabr', ex-leg-spinner Stuart MacGill has now admitted to using sandpaper on the ball during his playing career. MacGill, who played 44 Tests and three ODIs for Australia between 1998 and 2008, said he had used sandpaper on the ball but insisted that it was not part of a bigger plan to cheat. His admission has added another twist to the Sandpapergate controversy, which took place during Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. The incident had led to bans for three Australian players and remains one of the biggest controversies in Australian cricket. MacGill reveals how he used sandpaper Speaking to former Sydney Sixers teammates Steve O'Keefe and Moises Henriques on a FanaticsTV YouTube show, MacGill explained how he would attach a small piece of sandpaper to his thumb and use it to scratch the ball. "I'd cut a small piece of sandpaper and tape it to my thumb," he said. "It was not a part of a massive 'global cheating scam'; I was just really curious to see what would happen and if it would work. And oh, it works (laughs)," said MacGill. He also explained how he would use the sandpaper after tea, remove it from his thumb and throw it away before the match continued. "What they would do is the umpires as you're walking out on the ground, they used to put the ball sort of about 20 metres over the boundary and leave it there and you'd run out on the field, pick it up and go on the field. I would tape a little bit of a square of sandpaper on my thumb, pick the ball up just after tea, scratch the living daylights out of it, pull the sandpaper off, chuck it in the gutter before a ball had even been bowled. So nobody even knew that I'd done it, apart from all the scratches on the ball," he added. — thefanatics (@thefanatics) Khawaja's claims reopen Sandpapergate MacGill's admission comes after Khawaja made fresh claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in his memoir, 'Sabr'. Cricket Australia has maintained that the wider Australian team was not aware of the plan to use sandpaper to change the condition of the ball during the Cape Town Test against South Africa. However, Khawaja's revelations have raised fresh questions about what other players knew about the incident. Darren Lehmann, who was Australia's head coach during the 2018 tour of South Africa, has strongly denied knowing about the plan to use sandpaper. Players such as Mitchell Starc have also publicly denied any involvement in the scandal. Former Australia captain David Warner, one of the three players punished over the incident, has backed Khawaja and said that the claims in his autobiography are true.

item.title: Mason Miller Sweeps NL Reliever of the Year Votes for Padres
item.description: Mason Miller Padres Getty San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller was named the winner of the inaugural National League Reliever of the Year Award. Miller, the game’s premier closer, was about as close to a lock to win an MLB award as you’ll ever see, and that’s exactly what happened when the award was announced on Wednesday night. Mason Miller Wins Unanimously The BBWAA shared the vote totals, with Miller earning all 30 first-place votes for 210 total points. In second place was Philadelphia Phillies closer Jhoan Duran, who finished with 110 points, and third place was Trevor Megill of the Milwaukee Brewers, who had 66 points. Miller is the game’s best relief arm, and everyone knew he would win this award. The only question is whether he got every first-place vote from every voter, and that’s exactly what happened, as all the voters unanimously agreed he was the National League’s best reliever in 2026. Padres Closer Was Outstanding This season, Miller pitched to a 1.67 ERA with a league-leading 38 saves for the Padres. He pitched in 66 games, with 70 IP and an outstanding 129 strikeouts, while racking up 3.1 bWAR. It was just an absolutely amazing year for Miller, who came over from the Athletics in 2025 in a blockbuster trade. Despite being one of the best pitchers in baseball, Miller’s name will likely be on the trade block once again if the Padres feel like they can get an even bigger haul for him in a trade than what they dealt for him. Now, the question is whether the Padres will cash in on Miller as a trade chip , or keep him as their closer next season. While it’s an easy decision to keep Miller since he is such a great pitcher, the Padres could likely get a haul back from another squad if they did end up moving him, as every other team in the league would surely love to have him closing games for their team. That being said, the Padres are one of the top teams in the NL, so it makes sense for them to keep Miller and hope they can make a deep playoff run next season.
